sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P And 2 Others Counsel for Applicant :-
Anil Kumar Mishra Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Sandeep Kumar Chaurasiya Hon'ble Mrs. Manju Rani Chauhan,J.

Heard Sri Anil Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Akhilesh Kumar Srivastava,
learned A.G.A. for the State and Sri Sandeep Kumar Chaurasiya, learned counsel appearing for the informant.

The application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been preferred to quash entire proceedings of Case No. 1295 of 2022 in Case Crime No. 30 of 2021, under Sections 147, 498A, 352, 323, 504, 506 IPC,
Police Station Kotwali Nagar, District Saharanpur, chargesheet dated 01.3.2021 and summoning order dated 20.6.2022 passed by II A.C.J. (S.D.) / A.C.J.M., Saharanpur.
Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the parties have reconciled their differences and a compromise deed has been entered between them.

In this regard, a compromise deed on behalf of both the parties has been moved before the concerned court mentioning therein that parties have Vikramjeet And 5 Others vs State Of U.P And 2 Others on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181367821/
1 entered into compromise and do not want to press the case, copy of said compromise deed has been annexed as Annexure No. 3 to this application.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, no useful purpose would be served in continuing the proceedings before the court below and the same is not only sheer wastage of time of the Court but also abuse of the process of law.

Learned A.G.A., however, submits that it is the concerned court below, which has to verify the fact as to whether the parties have entered into compromise, hence the parties may approach the concerned court below and move an application with respect to compromise between the parties,
which will be decided in accordance with law.

In view of the above, both the parties are directed to appear before the court below along with a certified copy of this order within two weeks from today and be permitted to file a proper compromise deed.

It is expected that the trial court may fix a date for the verification of the compromise and after ensuring the presence of parties, pass an appropriate order with respect to the same in accordance with law, as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of two months from today.

While passing the order verifying the compromise, the concerned court shall also record the statements of the parties as to whether all the terms and conditions mentioned in the original compromise deed, so filed, have been fulfilled or not.

The court in that scenario will allow the parties to obtain certified copy of the report as well as compromise and it will be open for the applicants to approach this Court again for quashing of the proceedings.

For the period of two months or till decision on the aforesaid application so filed by applicant,
whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant in the aforesaid case.
With the aforesaid observations and directions, the application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. is disposed of.
